newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gets U.S. fuel to help bring in harvest.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gets U.S. fuel to help bring in harvest.

text.p: Ukraine took shipment on late Monday of 34,000 tonnes of diesel and gasoline from the United States to help bring in this year's harvest, an American government official said on Tuesday.
"This is not a gift, it's a credit," Gregory Huger, director of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Ukraine mission, told a news conference in the Black Sea port of Odessa.
The fuel shipment, from Mobil Corp, will be transported to six farming provinces by Interagro, a private Ukrainian company.
Ukraine is using a total $175 million USAID credit to buy large amounts of fuel, equipment and chemicals.
Huger said $50 million would be used for fertilisers and herbicides and the rest to purchase fuel.
Ukraine's grain harvest is forecast at a low 28 million tonnes this year.
Drought is blamed, but shortages of fuel and machinery have also taken their toll on the sector. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
